pr.body:
**What is this feature?**

Writes to annotations are sometimes rejected on MySQL due to a recurring deadlock with the annotation cleanup job.
Details here: https://github.com/grafana/grafana/issues/64979

**Why do we need this feature?**

The deadlock seems to be a result of the subquery, under normal circumstances a plain insert and delete should not lock, and there are no extended transactions at play.

This PR splits the subquery into a separate SQL statement. These statements do not share a transaction, and therefore allow locks to flush in between.

Unfortunately we could not reduce this to a single DELETE statement, due to the batching - DELETE LIMIT is not supported on all databases without needing to reintroduce the subquery. The IDs loaded into memory are of bounded size due to the batch size configuration.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**:

https://github.com/grafana/grafana/issues/64979

**Special notes for your reviewer:**

Please check that:
- [x] It works as expected from a user's perspective.
- [x] If this is a pre-GA feature, it is behind a feature toggle.
- [x] The docs are updated, and if this is a [notable improvement](https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/writing-guide/contribute-release-notes/#how-to-determine-if-content-belongs-in-a-whats-new-document), it's added to our [What's New](https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/writing-guide/contribute-release-notes/) doc.

validated_findings.trigger: A regression occurs only when a single DELETE would receive more than SQLite 3.32's 32,766-variable limit.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 99 shows createAnnotationsNum=40003 distributed across 3 annotation types (alert, dashboard, API), so each type gets ~13334 rows. The test claims to verify SQLite's 32766 limit but never actually fetches that many IDs in one batch, making the boundary test ineffective.

validated_findings.body: The added tests seed rows before invoking cleanup and only add a SQLite-oriented boundary case, so they do not verify that concurrent MySQL inserts avoid the original deadlock or that no annotations are incorrectly lost.
validated_findings.failure_mode: CI can accept an implementation that passes functional SQLite cleanup tests while still deadlocking on the target MySQL path.
validated_findings.impact: The added tests seed rows before invoking cleanup and only add a SQLite-oriented boundary case, so they do not verify that concurrent MySQL inserts avoid the original deadlock or that no annotations are incorrectly lost.
validated_findings.root_cause: The revised integration test remains entirely sequential despite the production change being motivated by a database concurrency failure.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add a MySQL integration test using separate connections that overlaps annotation insertion with batched cleanup and asserts both operations complete without deadlock and preserve the expected rows.
validated_findings.title: The MySQL deadlock fix lacks a concurrent-write regression test
validated_findings.trigger: Cleanup runs on MySQL while another connection inserts annotations, which is the execution path the query split is intended to repair.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim about missing MySQL deadlock regression tests is a test coverage suggestion rather than a defect introduced by the patch. The patch's stated purpose is to fix deadlocks; absence of a concurrent test is a pre-existing test gap, not a patch-introduced bug.

validated_findings.body: The comment incorrectly presents 999 as SQLite's universal limit even though SQLite 3.32 raised the default SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER to 32,766, obscuring why the code intentionally uses a conservative threshold.
validated_findings.evidence: // SQLite has a parameter limit of 999.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Maintainers receive stale compatibility information when reasoning about the deletion strategy.
validated_findings.impact: The comment incorrectly presents 999 as SQLite's universal limit even though SQLite 3.32 raised the default SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER to 32,766, obscuring why the code intentionally uses a conservative threshold.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new comment describes a version-dependent default as an unconditional database limit.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: State that 999 is the default limit for older supported SQLite versions or a conservative compatibility threshold, and mention the newer default where relevant.
validated_findings.title: SQLite parameter-limit comment is incorrect for current SQLite
validated_findings.trigger: A maintainer evaluates or changes this workaround for SQLite 3.32 or newer.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 605 states "SQLite has a parameter limit of 999" but SQLite 3.32+ raised SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER to 32766 by default. The comment is factually incorrect for modern SQLite versions and misleads maintainers about why 999 is used.

validated_findings.body: No cleanup callback has yet been registered, so the shared fakeSQL database retains partial annotations and tags; later table cases can then fail from explicit-ID collisions or incorrect counts, obscuring the original failure.
validated_findings.failure_mode: A setup failure contaminates subsequent table-driven cases and causes cascading test failures.
validated_findings.impact: No cleanup callback has yet been registered, so the shared fakeSQL database retains partial annotations and tags; later table cases can then fail from explicit-ID collisions or incorrect counts, obscuring the original failure.
validated_findings.root_cause: The patch moved cleanup ownership into each subtest but places registration after all fixture setup and initial assertions.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Register the annotation and annotation_tag cleanup callback at the beginning of each subtest, before creating or asserting any fixture data.
validated_findings.title: Subtest cleanup is registered only after setup can fail
validated_findings.trigger: createTestAnnotations or either initial database assertion fails after partially inserting rows.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The t.Cleanup registration at line 120 occurs after createTestAnnotations and assertions, but Go's t.Cleanup runs in LIFO order at subtest end regardless of registration timing. If setup fails, the test fails immediately; cleanup still runs. The claimed contamination scenario is not how Go testing works.
